public_lecture_sections.lecture_title: Lecture 1: Membranes as selective chemical boundaries

modules.explanation: A phospholipid bilayer is a chemical boundary because hydrophilic head groups face water while hydrophobic tails form an internal non-polar core. Small non-polar molecules cross more easily than ions because charged solutes must shed hydration shells and enter an energetically unfavourable core.

blocks.content: Permeability is not absolute: transport proteins change the effective boundary for specific ions or polar solutes.

public_lecture_sections.lecture_title: Lecture 2: Transport proteins convert gradients into flux

modules.module_title: Electrochemical gradients combine concentration and voltage
modules.explanation: An electrochemical gradient has a concentration component and an electrical component. A cation may move down its concentration gradient but against the membrane voltage, so the direction of net movement depends on the combined free-energy difference rather than concentration alone.

blocks.label: Worked example
blocks.content: For an ion, compare the chemical term with the voltage term before predicting net flux direction.
